title: Karnataka HC on EPS-95: What the Pension Ruling Means for You
description: The Karnataka High Court has upheld the existing amendments to the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995 (EPS-95). This ruling rejects the plea from a group of reti.

faq.a: EPS-95, or the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995, is a social security scheme managed by EPFO. It provides a monthly pension to employees in the organised sector upon retirement, disability, or to their families in case of the employee's demise.

faq.q: What did the Karnataka HC ruling say?
faq.a: The Karnataka High Court upheld the amendments made to the EPS-95 scheme, particularly those introduced in 2014. This means it validated the ₹15,000 monthly pensionable salary cap and the provisions for pension reduction in case of early retirement.

faq.q: Does this mean I cannot get a higher pension?
faq.a: For the time being, yes. The ruling reinforces the ₹15,000 cap on pensionable salary for EPS-95 calculations. Unless a higher court overturns this decision, your EPS-95 pension will be calculated based on this maximum limit.

faq.q: How is the EPS pension calculated?
faq.a: The monthly pension is generally calculated using the formula: (Pensionable Salary × Service Years) / 70. The 'Pensionable Salary' is capped at ₹15,000 per month, irrespective of your actual basic salary.

faq.q: What is the maximum pension I can get from EPS-95?
faq.a: With the ₹15,000 pensionable salary cap, and assuming a maximum service period of 35 years (after 20 years of service, an additional 2 years are added for calculation), the maximum pension would be (₹15,000 × 35) / 70 = ₹7,500 per month.

faq.q: What if I contributed on a higher salary?
faq.a: Even if your employer contributed to your EPF account based on a basic salary higher than ₹15,000, the portion diverted to EPS-95 for pension calculation purposes is still capped at ₹15,000 as per the current rules and the recent court ruling.

faq.q: Is there any recourse for affected retirees?
faq.a: While the Karnataka High Court has upheld the amendments, legal challenges regarding EPS-95 have seen varying outcomes across different courts. Affected parties may explore options for appeal to higher judicial forums, such as the Supreme Court, for a final resolution.
